subject: Banking
title: The Panama Papers
description: A quick win: understand The Panama Papers.

hook.text: 11.5 million documents leaked from law firm Mossack Fonseca.

buildup.text: Banks created shell companies in Panama, the British Virgin Islands.

discovery.text: The Papers exposed heads of state, celebrities, and criminals using the same offshore structures.

twist.text: Iceland's prime minister resigned within days. But most countries did nothing.

climax.text: The Panama Papers showed that tax evasion is a service that banks sell.

punchline.text: 11.5 million leaked files. One PM resigned. Most offshore money stayed hidden.

quiz.question: What did the Panama Papers reveal?
options: How banks helped the wealthy hide money in offshore shell companies

details.summary: The 2016 Panama Papers leak revealed how banks helped wealthy clients use offshore shell companies to hide assets, evade taxes, and launder money through Panama law firm Mossack Fonseca's global network.
details.whyItMatters: The Panama Papers showed that offshore tax evasion is not a fringe activity but a systematic service offered by mainstream banks to their wealthiest clients, costing governments billions in lost tax revenue.
takeaways: 11.5 million documents from Mossack Fonseca were leaked in 2016
Over 500 banks created offshore companies through the firm
World leaders, celebrities, and criminals were named in the documents

faq.question: Did the Panama Papers lead to criminal prosecutions?
faq.answer: Several countries launched investigations. Iceland's prime minister resigned, and numerous individuals were charged with tax evasion. Mossack Fonseca shut down in 2018, and its founders were charged with money laundering.

faq.question: Is offshore banking always illegal?
faq.answer: No. Holding assets offshore is legal if properly reported to tax authorities. The scandal exposed that many clients deliberately hid offshore holdings to evade taxes, crossing the line from legal tax planning to criminal evasion.
